newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila suspends onshore NDF dlr sales for 3 mths.
newsitem.headline: Manila suspends onshore NDF dlr sales for 3 mths.

text.p: The Philippine central bank has barred onshore banks from selling non-deliverable forward dollars to offshore counterparties for the next three months, bank officials said on Thursday.
Governor Gabriel Singson said the suspension was to allow the central bank to review the legality and practice of the derivative instrument.
The suspension will take effect as soon as a circular is sent to banks. Central bank officials have yet to finalise the date of its release.
Central bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes told reporters the suspension was only for dollar sales.
"What is being regulated right now is the outflow of dollars," he said.

NDFs are forward contracts between two banks, usually one onshore and one offshore. The profit or loss is made on the difference between the contracted prices. The underlying currency does not change hands.
"It's up for review ... The agreement with the BAP (Bankers Association of the Philippines) is to clear up things," Singson told reporters.
The review of the NDF was recommended by the BAP after the recent speculative attack on the peso, which some bankers claimed was exacerbated by the forward transactions.
Singson said a more definitive policy statement is expected to be formulated in the coming months.
Eight local and foreign bank branches have derivative licences which allow them to engage in peso-dollar NDFs.
